title: Quantum thermodynamics and semidefinite optimization: Boltzmann, Fermi-Dirac, and Bose-Einstein frameworks
authors: Michele Minervini, Nana Liu, Dhrumil Patel, Mark M. Wilde
abstract: Here we argue how quantum thermodynamics offers a unifying interpretation for a wide class of semidefinite programs (SDPs) that arise in quantum information. Three SDP variable constraints, namely trace-one density operators, operator-bounded measurements, and the unbounded positive semidefinite cone, admit thermodynamic regularizations associated with Boltzmann, Fermi-Dirac, and Bose-Einstein statistics, respectively. In each case the entropy-regularized dual is unconstrained and concave in a chemical-potential vector, and the primal optimum is a thermal operator of the matched statistics. The dual gradient and Hessian are thermal expectation values, enabling hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for solving a wide variety of SDPs.
summary: This work unifies the mathematical structure of quantum information problems (SDPs) by interpreting them through the lens of quantum thermodynamics. It demonstrates that Boltzmann, Fermi-Dirac, and Bose-Einstein statistics each provide a natural, solvable regularization for different types of quantum constraints. This yields hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for solving complex quantum optimization problems.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a unified thermodynamic framework to interpret various Semidefinite Programs (SDPs) that arise in quantum information theory.
main_result: It shows that three distinct statistical ensembles—Boltzmann, Fermi-Dirac, and Bose-Einstein—each provide a natural thermodynamic regularization for different types of SDP constraints, leading to a common mathematical structure.
method: The approach involves using free-energy regularization and Lagrangian duality to transform constrained SDPs into unconstrained, concave dual optimization problems parameterized by chemical potentials.
model_or_system: The analysis covers quantum systems governed by three statistical frameworks: Boltzmann (for state variables), Fermi-Dirac (for measurement operators), and Bose-Einstein (for general PSD operators). The optimization is governed by a grand canonical Hamiltonian.
key_observables: The dual gradient and Hessian are shown to be closed-form as thermal expectation values, which are the key quantities for algorithm implementation.
important_parameters: Temperature (T) acts as a continuous control parameter, allowing the method to smoothly approximate the original, hard-constrained SDPs.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the system can be treated at a finite temperature T>0 to obtain a smooth approximation of the original SDP. For the BE case, it assumes the Hamiltonian is gapped.
figures_summary: Table I summarizes the three frameworks, detailing the feasible set, entropy, relative entropy, and the form of the primal optimum for Boltzmann, FD, and BE statistics.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general thermodynamic regularization for SDPs, then details the specific mathematical and algorithmic implementations for the Boltzmann, Fermi-Dirac, and Bose-Einstein cases, culminating in a discussion of hybrid quantum-classical solvers.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, unifying mathematical tool that connects the abstract optimization problems of quantum information theory directly to fundamental concepts of statistical mechanics (thermal expectation values, chemical potentials).
